utterances.text: It should be Exhibit 610. I'm sorry. No, it's -- perhaps it's 29. THE USHER: Twenty-nine?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we've previously noted in our discussion of the route of the column, in many instances the route of the column, that they followed, was dictated by the terrain and where the hills were. Yet when you look at this particular set of stories, essentially while the major terrain features run in ridges along this way, the statements would have you believe that these four individuals essentially crossed a long series of ridges and hills in order to try and reach friendly lines from way up here. Further, when you look at the four witness statements and compare them with each other, in almost all respects, it's obvious that the witness statements themselves are identical, to a point where the author got very lazy and essentially copied the route and path and circumstances of all four individuals. If you lay them up against each other, the series of circumstances are almost identical, which would further lead me to believe that the recounting didn't happen the way it did. It's almost too perfect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the story that they recount after getting up into the area where they were captured?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The story, as it is recounted in those statements, is that they got up into this area, and where their actual trek took them was in this direction here, somewhere in this region right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the area.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very mountainous area in the 1st Battalion sector, I believe it's referred to as Donji Lokanj. I know I've killed the pronunciation there. I'm sorry. But in that area there, they came across two -- one soldier of the 1st Battalion, who provided them food and water, and his son who came in later and also assisted. However, as these survivors -- as these prisoners were seen by other people, what happened was that word got back to the Zvornik Brigade and these four people were taken into custody. Their statements were generated to use for legal purposes against the two Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can have a seat. Let's discuss briefly the exhibits where you get this story. The first one, I believe, is Exhibit 706. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is from the Assistant Commander for Security for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, discussing that as a result of his initial investigation, the two individuals in question, one Nesko Dzokic and one Slobodan Dzokic, are to be held in detention for three days until the Military Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina can determine what they want to do with these individuals. And the explanation discusses the broad series of events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Dzokics are the Serb soldiers that were apparently arrested for providing food to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from this mention of up to three days' detention, were there any records to indicate what eventually happened to these two Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't have any information on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to Exhibit 707. Is this one of the statements from one of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the statements from one of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular individual, Sakib Kiviric, was from the village of Jagonje, in the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. I would just also note, on the original document, the signature of the individual and the signature of the individual who took the statement, who is in fact a member of the Zvornik Military Police Company, Crime Prevention Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has that got an exhibit -- that's the same exhibit we've referred to before?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is 707A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know roughly how far the Branjevo Military Farm is from this Donji Lokanj, the area of the headquarters of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly four kilometres, five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the exhibit -- let's go to the next exhibit, 708A. What does this illustrate, and how do you fit it in to your overall analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Leaving that aspect and going back into the aspect of Muslims being captured as a result of military activity, the first series of paragraphs notes what they're doing. It also notes the fact that they're capturing Muslims still. But for the first time, in paragraph 3, is a request that the Corps Command, or through the Corps Command, that the exchange submission start work as soon as possible, and requiring instructions on what to do with prisoners that they're taking, where to put them and who to hand them over to. So for the first time on July 22, 1995, the Zvornik Infantry Brigade is now requesting from the Drina Corps instructions on what to do with Muslim prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates that somewhere along the time frame prior to 22 July there was some form of a directive or some form of guidance change on what the disposition would be of Muslim prisoners captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. What do you mean, "guidance change"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: An order or directive that indicates that from a certain point in time there will be a change in what happens with the Muslim prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Butler, we'll now get into the time period of September 1995, where, to remind Your Honours, the aerial images show disturbances at the mass grave Branjevo Farm, for example, on the latter part of September -- I believe September 27th, but in the latter part of September -- and all the movement and the secondary graves. Mr. Butler, we have seen over the last several days all kinds of documents, engineering documents, for example, military police documents, related to the crime scenes at Orahovac, at Branjevo Farm, at Kozluk, at Petkovci. The engineering log that you referred to many times, to what date did that log go to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, and my memory may be unclear on this one, but I believe that the log goes out to 10 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, from the Bratunac Brigade or the Zvornik Brigade, do you have any similar records for the period of September, what we're referring to as the removal of the bodies from the primary mass graves, any indications like we did for the July period?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part we have the same bodies of information, which obviously the Office of the Prosecutor seized throughout the entire period. But when we look at the material for September/October of 1995, we do not see the same reflections of activity at all. We don't see the expected activities with the engineer equipment for fuel utilisation and vehicle utilisation during those periods; we don't see those types of activities rolled up at all in the daily combat or interim combat reports for those periods. We have very few pieces of information which can possibly be linked to the known reburial activities that took place during the period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there are a couple of documents that you have; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a few documents which we can associate with the reburial activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to Exhibit 709A. Tell us what this is, who it's from, and how you evaluate it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular document is from the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, 14 September 1995, to the Drina Corps Command, to the Main Staff Logistics Sector, with a copy to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade for their information. What it discusses is approval by the Main Staff, under the signature of General Mladic, for 5 tonnes of diesel fuel for the carrying out of engineer work in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps. It notes that the fuel will be delivered directly to the Standard barracks in Zvornik and put under the custody of Captain Milorad Trpic, T-r-p-i-c. It further notes that that individual will be responsible for the accurate maintenance of records on the number of engine work hours of engineering machines and account accordingly for consumption of fuel. When reviewing the name of Captain Milorad Trpic, there is no Captain Milorad Trpic assigned to the Zvornik Infantry Brigade; however, there is a Captain Milorad Trbic, T-r-b-i-c, and he is an officer assigned to the security organ of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. So assuming that that is the individual who they mean, what this order is doing is that rather than placing the logistics and the technical services people in charge of fuel, this particular fuel is being placed in the custody or accountable to an officer in the Security Branch of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's the author of this document, based on the document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's under the signature of General Mladic, the Commander of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would a security officer normally be in charge of fuel for engineering works?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally fuel accountability is the responsibility of the Rear Services Branch, the Technical Services Directorate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what's your analysis regarding what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that when we look at the engineer vehicle utilisation logs for September and October and we don't see this type of work reflected in the Zvornik Brigade engineer equipment, when I look at this, the theory that comes to me -- and again this is one piece of information -- is that Captain Trbic has been appointed to ensure that the fuel goes out to the required engineer equipment, that he accounts for the material, but this is a separate series of fuel usage and accounting from the rest of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you think this fuel may have been used for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period in question, the overhead images clearly show the reburial activity. We know that, as a fact, happened. During the same period, the Zvornik Brigade reports, notes, road building activity during a good percentage of this period. We don't have information which would confirm the road building theory or the road building activity. Based on that in isolation, I would have to say that this fuel was used for the reburial activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit 710A. It's a related exhibit. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This essentially is the 35th logistics base instructing the Drina Corps Command and the Zvornik Brigade Command that the diesel fuel is available and that a Drina Corps representative shall collect the fuel and provide the transportation. I'm sorry. It's not from the 35th logistics base, it's from the logistics sector to the logistics base and info the Drina Corps Command and Zvornik Infantry Brigade Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14 September 1995, who is the Commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, the Commander of the Drina Corps is Major General Krstic -- General Major Krstic, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to Exhibit 711A, this appears to be a log reflecting Milorad Trbic; is that correct? I believe on the --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 33 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on the first page, reflecting him as a member of the Brigade Command Security Branch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's at least one document from the Bratunac Brigade in our exhibit list, Exhibit 712A. Can you tell us what this document is, what kind of book it came out of, and how it fits in to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This specific document is a journal that was maintained to record morning or periodic meetings where the Brigade Commander addressed what he refers to as his Corps Command staff, those being his primary assistant commanders and deputies and, in some cases, the subordinate battalion commanders. Depending on the combat situation or the events, these meetings occurred daily; in some cases twice a day; and in some cases, like during the operation at Bratunac with Srebrenica, there were three- or four- or five-day gaps. What this book and several others like it, because this book is very fragmentary in its dates, reflected are the orders and the directives and the issues that were raised at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the information on this exhibit are you referencing as part of your analysis on the secondary grave or the robbing aspect?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that particular aspect, there is a notation reflecting the 16 October 1995 meeting and the individuals present. If you look down to the block pertaining to Nikolic, who is again Captain First Class Momir Nikolic, the Assistant Commander for Intelligence and Security at the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, he notes two things: first, that they're still continuing to capture Muslim men who are trying to remain in the area near their houses, and the last item is an acknowledgment to the staff and the Commander of the brigade that they are currently engaged in tasks issued by the army of Republika Srpska General Staff or Main Staff; in parenthesis is the phrase "(asanacija)" which is terrain restoration or sanitation. We've seen that phrase before with regard to the 15 July interim combat report. It directly relates to the burying of bodies. And looking at the B/C/S version of that, the word in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, that's a fairly vague reference there. Are you aware of an aerial image taken at Glogova on 20 October at the mass grave site there of a loader digging at that time, some four days after this October 16th report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I also want to call your attention to -- Mr. Nikolic says that this was a task issued by the General Staff or the Main Staff of the VRS. How do you account for this suggestion that the Main Staff has been given a task directly, perhaps, to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the scope of how I understand orders are passed down, I don't interpret it as a direct order from the Main Staff to the Bratunac Brigade. The presumption that I would make is that the order originated from the Main Staff, that it came through the Drina Corps to the Bratunac Brigade. And while it may have come through security channels, Captain First Class Nikolic as working for the Brigade Command and Commander are advising all of them as to the contents of this order. Having said that, I can't discount the possibility, because it doesn't specifically say that, that this order directly came from the Main Staff to the Bratunac Brigade, but of relevance, it's being briefed to the Commander of the Bratunac Brigade. The presumption being if this order somehow missed the Drina Corps, that Colonel Blagojevic would be empowered to call up the Drina Corps command and ask, what are we doing and why are we doing it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the previous exhibits, we saw that General Mladic of the Main Staff dealing with the Zvornik Brigade Milorad Trbic; however, it was done indirectly, of course by chain of command through the Drina Corps. Is that the normal way this should work?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't have the documents that may reflect how this particular job was assigned or what particular job this was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be normal for a commander to not know of such activity occurring in his zone that must have taken days to occur, just to briefly summarise, the movement of some 3500 to 5500 bodies from several mass graves both in Zvornik and Bratunac areas, to many areas, secondary graves throughout the entire area. Would it be normal for a commander not to have any idea that was happening in his area at this time period?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Particularly with respect to this time period, and under a declared state of war that now exists, and the fact that most of the areas in question fall into the designated war zones where the military has exclusive primacy based on the scope of activity that had to have occurred and one would assume primarily at night for the burial operations and the movement of the remains, the different locations and all the assets that needed to happen with that, I would be very hard pressed to come up with any form of an explanation on how the Drina Corps staff, in general, and how the Drina Corps Commander, specifically, could not have been aware of what was going on over, essentially, a two-month period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who, Mr. Butler, is in the best position to know the lay of the land, to know the geography, to know the places to hide bodies, to be able to get the equipment and the manpower to do it, to secure the routes, to secure the roads, to do all the things that must be necessary for such an operation? Who is in the best position to do that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of the burial and reburial activity in the Zvornik Brigade, the logical conclusion is the Commander of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. He is responsible for the land. He is responsible for the security of that land. He has the manpower to accomplish the mission. He has the engineer equipment assigned to him to accomplish the mission. He's in the position to do those activities as well as continue combat-related activities as they should occur. It's all within the functions of and within the purview of the Brigade Commander of the Zvornik Brigade. In the case of those that occurred in the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade zone, the same rationale would apply with the possible exception of the engineer equipment which the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade did not own. But again, because of the prevailing state of war, it certainly would have been within the purview of the Rear Services Branch of the Bratunac Brigade to requisition whatever equipment that they would have needed to do this from the local economy. But at the end of the day, the people most qualified to do this and best equipped to do it would be the respective brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in order to dig up thousands of bodies, you have to know where to look if they're all under the ground by mid-September 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an implied, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without going through the evidence again, it -- it's clear that the elements of the Zvornik Brigade know where the bodies are buried in their area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering that they put them there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this brings to a close this portion of the direct testimony. We have other testimony and according to our original plan, it would be appropriate at this time to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going into closed session. We do not have conditions here for the public to be present, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, there is one more little video Mr. Harmon reminded me of that should be in open session. It won't take long. If we could play that in open session then we'll be ready to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So we'll remain in open session to see this video and only later will we go into closed session. So open session now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see any indication that we are in open session on the monitor. Is that all right now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The technical both has informed me that we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, fine thank you very much. You may continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we have a video, it's Exhibit 367. It starts out with a parade. It's a military get together of some sort. Can you tell the Court what this is and what's going on and the approximate date of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This video is the video coverage by the army of Republika Srpska and the Serbian radio and television network of a military ceremony that occurs in Vlasnica on I believe 2 or 5 December 1995. It relates to two things primarily. The first one being a speech by General Mladic about the recently-approved Dayton agreement, and the second part is to commemorate the establishment of a new formation within the army of the Republika Srpska. The mobile brigade, if you will, of the Drinski Corps. Essentially, in short, what they did is take the Drina Wolves formation with some other units and added some strength to it and created a separate formation that could be used anywhere across the territory of the Republika Srpska. What this ceremony depicts is the public establishment of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before we get to the video, we have an Exhibit 482A which is a Srpska Vojska article related to that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't that exhibit in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 482A, I've got a copy of that if that will save us some time. First of all, can you tell us what the Srpska Vojska is? You may have discussed that briefly in the past because I believe we had another article, but just again, could you remind us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srpska Vojska is the magazine of the army of Republika Srpska. Just like the Drina Corps had Drinski Magazin, this was the magazine of the entire army where events of general interest to the army were discussed in open form. This particular one, the magazine's article is dated 28 December, reflects the magazine's coverage, if you will, of the ceremony that we are discussing. For the purposes of the investigation, we didn't deal with obviously General Mladic's feelings towards Dayton, but at the back of his speech, he makes specific reference to the Drina Corps and the operations pertaining to Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about General Krstic, does he make any reference, in your view, to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, certainly not by name but by position. "You," and again to keep in mind, he's addressing the soldiers of the Drina Corps during this ceremony, "who fought under the leadership of your Chief of Staff or Corps Commander who although severely wounded made a tremendous contribution to the victory of the Serbian army." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French an English transcripts. So certainly within this context, and given the fact that General Krstic is up on the podium with him, the clear inference is that we are discussing General Major Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's a notation there, "... you who fought under as your Chief or your Commander," does that correspond with your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As my analysis is reflected during the period, during the actual capture of Srebrenica, General Major Krstic was the Chief of Staff of the Corps. During the actual operation to take over Zepa, he was the Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you -- the video portion that we are going to see does not have this section of the speech. Was that in possession or is that in possession, this section of the speech in the possession of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that we have the audio portion of that speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, we do have a portion of this ceremony, just a brief segment to give you a feel for who was there and General Mladic was at the podium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, who was there besides General Mladic and General Krstic that may relate to our case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There will be video coverage of two other individuals directly. One of them will be Captain First Class Milan Jolovic, who was the Commander of the Drina Wolves and was the designated Commander of this mobile brigade. And the second individual that will be seen in the video will be Colonel Beara the Chief of the Main Security Administration of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could play Exhibit 367, and it would help if the lights were lowered.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The individual now in the centre of the picture, that white-haired individual, was Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go back and play that again, booth?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, the technical both has informed me that they do not have lighting capabilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's fine. Is it possible just to go back to the very beginning? Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Butler, if you could just narrate this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you will see, General Mladic walking in. The man behind him is Colonel Beara, and General Krstic. The man he is saluting now is Captain First Class Milan Jolovic. You see General Krstic come into the picture you see Colonel Beara come into the picture. In the military sense this is General Mladic taking the salute of his troops accompanied by General Krstic and Captain First Class Jolovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have another exhibit, a still shot of that video that shows Colonel Beara, General Krstic, Captain Jolovic and General Mladic all in one frozen frame, that's Exhibit 65. And that was recently provided so it -- the Court should get copies, but I don't think we need to comment any further on that photo. And now after one false start, I believe we are ready to go into closed session and it may be helpful and productive to take a break now, Your Honours, so we can set up for the closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can have a break now. So we'll have a 30-minute break. I said 30 minutes. --- Break taken at 12.39 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I think that we will be here tomorrow morning again for the cross-examination. Mr. Petrusic, are you ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we will adjourn for today and come back again tomorrow morning at 9.30.
